subject: anaesthesia
title: Malignant Hyperthermia: Ryanodine Pathology, Dantrolene Therapy, and Airway Crises

steps.title: Ryanodine Receptor Gene Mutations
steps.tx: **Malignant hyperthermia pharmacogenetic pathology** is an autosomal dominant skeletal muscle channelopathy triggered by volatile inhalational anaesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane, isoflurane, halothane) or the depolarizing relaxant succinylcholine. Mutations in the skeletal ryanodine receptor gene (RYR1 on chromosome 19q13.1) or L-type voltage-gated calcium channel (CACNA1S) disrupt calcium channel regulation, causing massive uninhibited sarcoplasmic calcium release into the myoplasm.

steps.title: Hypermetabolic Clinical Cascade
steps.tx: **Hypermetabolic crisis of malignant hyperthermia** erupts as sustained intracellular calcium floods contractile myofibrils, driving continuous actin-myosin cross-bridging and overwhelming sarcoplasmic ATP pumps. Massive consumption of adenosine triphosphate generates extreme cellular hypermetabolism, manifesting as soaring carbon dioxide production (EtCO2 doubling unexpectedly), profound mixed metabolic-respiratory acidosis, generalized skeletal muscle rigidity, and secondary hyperpyrexia rising 1 to 2 degrees Celsius every five minutes.

rows: Earliest physical sign in spontaneously breathing patients
Excessive exothermic ATP hydrolysis in muscle
Core temperature spikes rapidly if untreated

steps.title: Masseter Muscle Spasm Herald Sign
steps.tx: **Masseter muscle spasm jaws of steel** describes acute contracture of the temporomandibular masseter muscles preventing mouth opening immediately following intravenous succinylcholine. While mild increased jaw stiffness occurs occasionally in normal children, complete inability to open the mouth signifies masseter spasm, serving as a critical herald warning that carries a 50 percent risk of evolving into fulminant malignant hyperthermia.

left.title: Normal Incomplete Relaxation
points: Mild resistance to manual jaw depression
Mouth can be opened with gentle upward force
Normal end-tidal carbon dioxide and heart rate

right.title: Pathological Masseter Spasm
points: Impenetrable trismus and jaw rigidity ('jaws of steel')
Cannot open mouth even with forceful laryngoscopy attempts
Demands halting elective surgery and monitoring for MH

steps.title: Dantrolene Sodium Emergency Protocol
steps.tx: **Dantrolene sodium specific antidote mechanism** binds directly to the RYR1 ryanodine receptor on the sarcoplasmic reticulum, blocking calcium release channels and halting uninhibited calcium efflux into the myoplasm. The initial intravenous dose is 2.5 milligrams per kilogram administered as a rapid push, repeated every 5 to 10 minutes until hypercapnia, muscle rigidity, and tachycardia subside, up to a maximal cumulative dose of 10 mg/kg.

nodes.label: Discontinue all volatile agents and succinylcholine immediately
Hyperventilate with 100% O2 at maximal fresh gas flows (>10 L/min)
Administer IV dantrolene sodium 2.5 mg/kg push via large-bore IV
Repeat 2.5 mg/kg boluses every 5-10 minutes until EtCO2 normalizes

steps.tx: This diagram follows the antidote to the exact channel it must close. Dantrolene binds the **ryanodine receptor** of skeletal muscle and damps the calcium flood that malignant hyperthermia unleashes from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Dosing is a chase rather than a recipe: two point five milligrams per kilogram pushed fast, repeated until carbon dioxide, rigidity and racing pulse surrender, sometimes to ten milligrams per kilogram. Reconstitution takes hands and time, which is why malignant hyperthermia trolleys drill the mixing as much as the medicine.
steps.say: Dantrolene blocks the ryanodine receptor to stop calcium flooding muscle in malignant hyperthermia.

steps.title: Ryanodex Formulations and Preparation
steps.tx: **Dantrolene preparation engineering advances** contrast classical dantrolene with modern nanocrystalline Ryanodex. Classical dantrolene (Dantrium) comes in 20-milligram glass vials containing 3 grams of mannitol; each vial requires reconstitution with 60 milliliters of sterile preservative-free water, requiring 36 vials and up to 20 minutes of vigorous shaking. Modern Ryanodex contains 250 milligrams of nanocrystalline suspension per vial, reconstituting in under one minute with 5 mL of water.

steps.title: Active Cooling and Supportive Care
steps.tx: **Supportive critical care in malignant hyperthermia** mandates active external and internal physical cooling: infuse iced 0.9 percent saline intravenously (avoid potassium-containing Ringer lactate), apply surface ice packs over groin, axillae, and neck, and perform cold gastric or bladder lavage, terminating active cooling once core temperature drops to 38.5 degrees Celsius to prevent overshoot hypothermia. Serial blood gases monitor for hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis.

left.title: Active Cooling Interventions
points: Infuse chilled intravenous normal saline (1,000 mL at 4C)
Apply ice bags to femoral, axillary, and carotid triangles
Halt active cooling once core temperature drops to 38.5C

right.title: Hyperkalaemia Management
points: Administer intravenous calcium chloride (10 mg/kg) to stabilize myocardium
Infuse 50 mL of 50% dextrose with 10 units regular insulin
Administer sodium bicarbonate (1-2 mEq/kg) for severe acidosis

steps.title: Aspiration Pneumonitis and Mendelson Syndrome
steps.tx: **Chemical aspiration pneumonitis pathogenesis** (Mendelson syndrome) occurs when acidic gastric juice is inhaled into the bronchial tree, destroying surfactant-producing type II pneumocytes and disrupting alveolar-capillary endothelial membranes within minutes. Treatment relies on immediate endotracheal suctioning before positive-pressure ventilation, supportive mechanical ventilation with PEEP, and bronchodilators; prophylactic antibiotics and high-dose steroids are strictly ineffective and unindicated.

rows: Direct chemical burn by sterile gastric acid (pH <2.5)
Inhalation of colonized oropharyngeal anaerobic bacteria
Immediate onset (within 1 to 2 hours of aspiration)
Purulent sputum, fever, new focal pulmonary infiltrate

steps.title: Acute Intraoperative Laryngospasm
steps.tx: **Acute laryngospasm emergency algorithm** reflects reflex adduction of laryngeal vocal cords and aryepiglottic folds mediated by the superior laryngeal nerve during light anaesthesia. Immediate management consists of removing surgical stimulation, applying jaw thrust with firm inward digital pressure at the Larson notch (laryngospasm notch behind the earlobe), delivering 100 percent oxygen via continuous positive airway pressure, and administering succinylcholine (0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg IV).

nodes.label: Identify inspiratory stridor or silent chest wall rocking
Cease surgical stimulation and clear pharyngeal secretions
Apply Larson notch bilateral digital pressure with CPAP 100% O2
Inject low-dose IV succinylcholine (0.2 mg/kg) if spasm persists
